C715282.title: A/R Collection groups customers by name, rows oldest date first

fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Customer B's group is above customer A's group.

Step 2:

  • "Date" is marked as the sorted column (a small arrow beside its heading).

Step 3:

  • The group opens: invoice A first (oldest date), then invoice B, then invoice C: on the same date the smaller number comes first, counted as a number, whatever the time of day each was invoiced.

What you should see today: in step 3, invoice B and invoice C, which have the same date, come out in the order they were invoiced that day, so invoice C comes before invoice B, instead of in invoice number order. This is a known problem and it is already reported — see https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-12138 (filed by Chris Ward on 3 Nov 2026).

· If you see exactly that, mark this test FAILED and do not raise anything new.

· If it fails in a DIFFERENT way from what is described above, that is a NEW problem — please report it.

· If it PASSES, the fix has shipped: report it so the ticket can be closed and this note removed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header)

  • S1-R6: “A/R Collection groups by customer and A/P Unpaid Invoices by vendor, groups in name order (S1-R2 to S1-R4); inside each group, rows open oldest date first; rows on the same date, whatever the time of day they were created, go in document-number order (S2-R4).”
  • S1-R7: “The column the report opened on is marked as sorted: the name column on the Summaries and Detail reports, the Date column on Collection and Unpaid Invoices.”
  • S2-R4: “ID and No. sort by number value: S1-99 before S1-100 before S1-101. The first click puts the smallest number first and the second click the largest first. The same number-aware order breaks ties in every sort, always smallest document number first: reversing a sort reverses the sorted column only, so tied rows keep that order in both directions. A date column compares the day only, never the time of day, so two rows on the same date are a tie.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p1-a-r-aging-summary-opens-a-to-z.png: figure "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"
  • ar-ap-p1-a-p-aging-detail-opens-by-vendor-name.png: figure "A/P Aging Detail opens by vendor name" (This build (after)), board "1. Opening order and header sorting"

The design's own words:

  • "Customer name order the way QuickBooks sorts ("10 Trucking" before "2 Trucking"), marked on the Customer header. S1-R1, S1-R2, S1-R4, S1-R7, S1-R8." (caption of "A/R Aging Summary opens A to Z")
  • "Buckets stay in fixed order; rows inside each bucket go by vendor name (was most overdue first). S1-R5, S2-R4, S2-R5." (caption of "A/P Aging Detail opens by vendor name")

Difference from the PRD (DD-04), closed: PRD version 5 said "inside each group, rows open oldest date first, ties by document number (S2-R4)" (S1-R6); the design shows in the CMLZ Truck Repair - Talladega group five invoices dated Aug 27, 2026 read S3-14690, S3-14693, S3-15660, S3-14691, S3-14692 (not number order). Chris Ward ruled on 23 Oct 2026 (answers 12 and 14): document-number order, as the PRD says, whatever the time of day the invoices were created; the current build orders same-day rows by time of day, a build bug to fix, and the design picture will be corrected. PRD version 9 (S1-R6, S2-R4) now says so, and this case follows it. The held design-version case D-79 (C715561) was deleted from TestRail on 26 Oct 2026 with the QA lead's go-ahead (snapshot in v9-pass-2026-10-26/deleted/).

C715416.title: A/R Detail: a work order invoice at another location asks to switch

fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • A dialog opens on the report, before leaving it.
  • Its title reads "Switch location?".
  • Its message reads "This work order is in " followed by location B's name and "Switch your active location to view it?".
  • The button "Cancel" is on the left and the button "Switch location" (small l) is on the right.
  • A close "×" is at the top right.

Step 2:

  • The work order's finance page opens.
  • The location switcher in the top right shows that your active location is now location B.

What you should see today: in step 1, the right-hand button of the "Switch location?" dialog reads "Switch Location" with a capital L instead of "Switch location". This is a known problem and it is already reported — see https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-12139 (filed by Chris Ward on 3 Nov 2026).

C154708.title: The Title label stays Title when a canned line is picked, then its text deleted

fields.title: The Title label stays Title when a canned line is picked, then its text deleted
fields.custom_steps:
1. Click New Line.
  2. Type the first three letters of canned line A's name.
  3. Click canned line A in the list.
  4. Click at the end of canned line A's name in the Title box.
  5. Press Backspace until the Title box is empty.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Line window opens over work order 1, with the cursor in the field labeled "Title".
  • The grey prompt "What are you doing?" shows inside the Title box, under the label.

Step 2:

  • The prompt is gone and only the three letters show.
  • The label still reads "Title".
  • Canned line A is offered in the list.

Step 3:

  • The field shows canned line A's name.
  • The label still reads "Title", not a question such as "What are you doing?".
  • No grey prompt sits beside the picked name.

Step 4:

  • The cursor sits at the end of canned line A's name, which still shows in the Title box.
  • No clear (x) button shows at the right end of the Title box.

Step 5:

  • The Title box is empty: canned line A's name is no longer picked.
  • The label still reads "Title".
  • The grey prompt "What are you doing?" shows again in the Title box.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "What Are You Doing / Why Are You Doing It?" (Title and Description), Confluence 845348896, version 17 (28 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 4 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11257, story SV-10130 (Story 1, The Work Order Line Dialog)

  • S1-R4: “The label does not change with the state of the field. It reads "Title" whether the canned-line picker is empty or filled, which replaces a rule that swapped the label between the question and "Title" depending on that state.”
  • S1-R5: “The canned-line picker at the top of the dialog is labeled "Title" and carries the placeholder "What are you doing?" in its typeahead box, the same as the free-text Title field. The dialog focuses this field on open, so the placeholder is visible the moment the dialog appears and clears as soon as the user types or picks a canned line. (Corrected 2026-09-10: the first build gave the picker no placeholder, so the prompt never appeared on a new line.)”
  • S1-R3: “The Title box carries the placeholder "What are you doing?" and the Description box carries "Why are you doing it?". Placeholder text shows while the box is empty and disappears as soon as there is a value. The labels Title and Description always sit at the top of their boxes, empty or filled, with the placeholder underneath; in production the label sat inside the empty box. This is the one layout change in the dialog.”
  • S1-R7: “Nothing else about the dialog changes, other than the label position in S1-R3: same fields in the same order, same validation, same values saved.”

From: Chris Ward, answer to question 16 in the What/Why question Doc (https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QcT7FRZci6AhYcI33HUac-Oob03-gCnCOKn2NFHMLjA), question posted 28 Oct 2026, read 4 Nov 2026

  • Answer 16: “No clear (x) button. A picked canned line is emptied the way it is today, by deleting its text in the Title box (Backspace). The picker is then empty again and the label still reads "Title" (S1-R4). An (x) would be a new control, and S1-R7 keeps the dialog as it is. Please test that deleting the text empties the picker.”
